issues.description: Default speaker for bulbul:v3-beta disagrees with its own documentation
issues.detail: The module docstring, class docstring, and PR description all state that `aditya` is the default speaker for bulbul:v3-beta. However, TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS sets default_speaker="shubh". A reader auditing this file cannot tell which is the intended invariant. Pick one and make the code and the prose agree; the literate-programming discipline is precisely that the explanation and the code must not contradict each other.
issues.lines: TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS bulbul:v3-beta entry vs. module docstring

issues.description: Pace clamping silently mutates user input; range check is incorrect when pace is None
issues.detail: The clamp logic warns and clamps when pace is outside [pace_min, pace_max], but `params.pace` has a Pydantic default of 1.0 and is Optional. The conditional `if pace is not None and (pace < pace_min or pace > pace_max)` is fine, but the invariant being enforced is asymmetric: a v3 user who explicitly requests 2.5 (legal for v2's range, illegal for v3) is silently clamped rather than rejected, while pitch/loudness/temperature outside their model are logged-and-ignored. State one invariant for out-of-range parameters and apply it uniformly: either reject (ValueError) or warn-and-clamp. Mixing the two is the kind of inconsistency a careful reader will trip on.

issues.description: `get_speakers_for_model` silently falls back to v2 speakers for unknown models
issues.detail: The function's contract per its docstring is "return speakers available for the model." Returning v2's speaker list for an unknown model is a lie that will produce confusing downstream errors when a caller hands one of those speakers to a v3 endpoint. Either raise ValueError on unknown models (matching the constructor's behavior) or return an empty list with a documented contract. Silent fallback violates the principle that the function's behavior should be statable in one sentence the caller can rely on.

issues.description: Ignored-parameter warnings fire on Pydantic defaults, not on user intent
issues.detail: Because `pitch`, `loudness`, and `temperature` have non-None Pydantic defaults (0.0, 1.0, 0.6), the heuristic `elif params.pitch != 0.0` only fires when the user explicitly diverges from the default. A user who passes `pitch=0.0` explicitly on v3 gets no warning; a user who passes `temperature=0.6` explicitly on v2 gets no warning. Use a sentinel (e.g., default=None with the real default applied later) so the warning reflects user intent rather than value-equality with the default. Minor, but the current code conflates "user supplied a parameter" with "value differs from default," which a careful reader will notice.

issues.description: MODEL_CONFIGS and TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS are module-level mutable Dicts typed as Dict, not Mapping
issues.detail: The dataclasses are `frozen=True` (good), but the outer registry is a plain `Dict[str, ...]`. A reader cannot tell from the type whether the registry is meant to be mutated at runtime (e.g., plugin registration) or frozen at import. Type as `Mapping[str, ...]` or wrap in `types.MappingProxyType` to make the invariant explicit. This is exactly the kind of "state the invariant" discipline that prevents future contributors from adding a `MODEL_CONFIGS["saaras:v4"] = ...` line at module load and breaking the type model.

issues.description: STT `_connect` removed `input_audio_codec` from connect_kwargs without explanation
issues.detail: The previous code sent `input_audio_codec` to the SDK's connect call; the new code drops it. There is no comment explaining whether the SDK no longer accepts the parameter, whether it's now inferred from another field, or whether this is a behavior change the caller should know about. For code that will be read later, a one-line literate comment ("v3 SDK infers codec from audio frames; pre-v3 SDKs ignored this kwarg") is the difference between an audit that passes and one that has to git-blame the change.

issues.description: Pydantic field declarations use `bool = None` which is type-incorrect
issues.detail: `vad_signals: bool = None` and `high_vad_sensitivity: bool = None` in InputParams are typed as `bool` but defaulted to `None`. They should be `Optional[bool] = None`. Pydantic v2 will likely catch this at model construction, but the declared type is wrong and a reader cannot infer intent. Pre-existing, but adjacent to this PR and worth fixing while the file is open.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT tendencies. The refactor to dataclass-based ModelConfig/TTSModelConfig is a real improvement: it replaces string-sniffing (`"saaras" in model.lower()`) with a single registry whose invariants — what each model supports, its defaults, its endpoint — are stated in one place. That is the right shape. The audit reveals three classes of issue worth fixing before merge: (1) the code and the docstrings disagree about the v3-beta default speaker (`aditya` in prose, `shubh` in the dict), which is the kind of contradiction literate-programming discipline exists to prevent; (2) the policy for out-of-range or model-incompatible parameters is inconsistent — pace gets warn-and-clamp, pitch/loudness/temperature get warn-and-ignore, language/mode/prompt get ValueError — pick one invariant and apply it uniformly; (3) several small literate-comment gaps (silent dropping of `input_audio_codec`, mutable Dict registries, Pydantic `bool = None`). No algorithmic complexity concerns — this is config-routing code, O(1) lookups throughout, no hot loops. The data structure choice (frozen dataclass + dict registry) is correct; finish the discipline by making the registries truly immutable and the prose match the data.
